subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The median voter theorem predicts that political parties in democracies will moderate their platforms to appeal to the centrist voter.
• Samir Kamau studied the 2019 Danish parliamentary election as a test case for the theorem.
• The election featured nine parties that won seats, with several maintaining distinctly non-centrist platforms.
• Kamau's analysis was published in 2021.
• Some political scientists have called the theorem "inapplicable to multiparty systems." Political analyst Nora Colombo defends it, writing that it "still illuminates coalition-building dynamics even in fragmented legislatures."
prompt: The student wants to use a quotation to refute the claim that the median voter theorem is inapplicable to multiparty systems. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: While some political scientists have called the median voter theorem "inapplicable to multiparty systems," others argue it "still illuminates coalition-building dynamics even in fragmented legislatures."
choices.B: Far from inapplicable, the median voter theorem "still illuminates coalition-building dynamics even in fragmented legislatures," as Colombo puts it, helping explain outcomes in elections like Denmark's 2019 parliamentary race.
choices.C: Given that the 2019 Danish election featured nine seat-winning parties with distinctly non-centrist platforms, the median voter theorem just might be "inapplicable to multiparty systems."
choices.D: Kamau's analysis of the 2019 Danish election "still illuminates coalition-building dynamics even in fragmented legislatures," as Colombo puts it.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer. By opening with 'Far from inapplicable' and then deploying Colombo's characterization of the theorem as something that 'still illuminates coalition-building dynamics even in fragmented legislatures,' the sentence directly refutes the claim that the median voter theorem is inapplicable to multiparty systems. The choice strengthens the refutation by pointing to a concrete example of the kind of election the theorem helps explain (Denmark's 2019 parliamentary race).
